questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

I. All P are Q.

II. Some Q are Z.

III. Some Z are T.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some T are P.

II. Some P are Z.

III. No T is Z.

options.text: Both conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bc0c2d565324cd271deabbcf4c17ed43dfb6dac9ff8517403fdd929c2622a889.png] 

**Conclusion:**

I. Some T are P → False (No direct relation given)

II. Some P are Z → False (No direct relation given)

III. No T is Z → False (Some Z are T)

Thus, None of the conclusions follow.

questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘RIP’ is written as ‘42’ and ‘MOL’ is written as ‘39’. What will be the code for ‘GAN’ in that code language?
questions.solution:
The logic follows here is:-

Add the place value of digit – 1

RIP → R + I + P = 18 + 9 + 16 – 1 = 43 – 1 = 42.

MOL → M + O + L = 13 + 15 + 12 – 1 = 40 – 1 = 39.

Similarly,

GAN → G + A + N = 7 + 1 + 14 – 1 = 22 – 1 = 21.

Thus, the correct answer is “21”.

questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘POLE’ is written as ‘48’ and ‘ROG’ is written as ‘40’. What will be the code for ‘TIP’ in that code language?
questions.solution:
The logic follows here is:-

Add the place value of digit

POLE → P + O + L + E = 16 + 15 + 12 + 5 = 48.

ROG → R + O + G = 18 + 15 + 7 = 40.

Similarly,

TIP → T + I + P = 20 + 9 + 16 = 45.

Thus, the correct answer is “45”.

questions.question:
Which two numbers need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

5 × 8 + 7 – 3 = 14
questions.solution:
The given equation is:-

5 × 8 + 7 – 3 = 14

Now, we have to be interchange and check.

1) 3 and 7 will be interchange then,

5 × 8 + 3 – 7 = 14

40 + 3 – 7 = 14

43 – 7 = 14

36 = 14.

2) 8 and 5

8 × 5 + 7 – 3 = 14

40 + 7 – 3 = 14

47 – 3 = 14

44 = 14

3) 8 and 3

5 × 3 + 7 – 8 = 14

15 + 7 – 8 = 14

22 – 8 = 14

14 = 14

So, option 3 is true, no need to check the 4th option,

Thus, the correct answer is “8 and 3”.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

I. Some wood are chairs.

II. All chairs are mats.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some mats are wood.

II. Some chairs are wood.

III. All wood are mats.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Both conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/35dcf3404a4fe7037249ddccfbbdf0b5a0e04abde4650e4d54a02b3da9a39b8d.png] 

**Conclusion:**

I. Some Mats are wood → True (Some word are chair and all chair are mats so those chair who is word is also mats)

II. Some Chairs are wood → True (Some word are chair)

III. All wood are mats → False (It can be possible)

Thus, Both conclusions I and II follow.

questions.question: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. 3 4 7
questions.solution:
The logic follows here is:-

Multiply the first and last digit of the column and add the second digit.

3 × 3 + 6 = 15

4 × 2 + 4 = 12

Similarly,

7 × 5 + 2 = **37**

Thus, the correct answer is “37”.

questions.question:
Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.

279, 277, 273, 267, ?
questions.solution:
The logic follows here is:-

279 – 2 = 277,

277 – 4 = 273,

273 – 6 = 267,

267 – 8 = **259**

Thus, the correct answer is “259”.
